title: StreetPulse™ — when the numbers stop making sense, ask the people behind them
description: StreetPulse puts your business question to up to 20 real consumers, on camera, in the street — and returns a boardroom-ready film in three weeks. The Miller Group’s proprietary research method.
slab: StreetPulse™ · The Miller Group’s proprietary method

hero.lede: Your messaging isn’t landing. Pricing is getting pushback. Sales have slowed and every department has a theory. The real answer isn’t in your data. It’s on the street, in the words of the people you’re trying to reach.
hero.rationale: Her own headline, her own opening paragraph — the strongest copy on millergroup.com today, and it sits on a page that is one nav item among seven. StreetPulse is the mechanism behind the site’s promise (“we find what’s holding your brand back”), so it earns a top-level page, its own gradient built from her brand palette, and a CTA that books time rather than asking for a form.

why.h2: Get out of the conference room.
paras: StreetPulse gets your team out of the conference room and into unscripted conversations with consumers, on camera, in high-traffic locations, reacting to the exact challenge keeping you up at night: messaging, pricing, product attributes, service, AI, whatever it is.

We turn these conversations into a boardroom-ready 2–3 minute video, built from up to 20 candid interviews and shaped by a moderator’s guide we develop from your stakeholder input. We get raw, unfiltered reactions to the questions we pose — and from there, consumer insights we share with your team.

In three weeks, you’ll have a clear, camera-verified read on what consumers understand, question, resist, and want next, plus a social-ready cut your team can use immediately. Questions we have put to the street:
questions: Celebrity-endorsed brands — do they work on you?
Name brand vs. generic: what are you actually paying for?
The Pink Tax — do you notice it?
Why did you stop shopping here?

steps.title: The question
steps.text: We sit with your stakeholders and write the moderator’s guide, so twenty conversations answer the thing your team is actually arguing about.

steps.title: The street
steps.text: Candid, on-camera intercepts in high-traffic locations with the shoppers your category depends on. No online panel, no incentivised click farm, no bots.

steps.title: The film
steps.text: A boardroom-ready 2–3 minute cut leadership will actually watch, the moment that changes the room time-stamped, plus the insights and a social-ready version.

facts.text: Real consumers, on camera, per engagement.
Built for the boardroom, not the archive.
Crew-shot footage with releases — usable as paid social the following week.

proof.h2: Two brands, two questions nobody could answer inside.
proof.sub: At Gelson’s, everyone assumed price. At Skirball, the brief was a younger, more diverse audience. Both started on the street.
proof.rationale: The only two StreetPulse results published anywhere on her site. The Gelson’s case is the whole positioning in one story.
